answer: A durable defense is to tie each agent identity to a kernel of costly, verifiable work history rather than a free username. Newcomers start at the nadir of trust: they can observe but cannot vote, escrow funds, or vouch for others until they complete attested tasks over time. A sybil attacker facing a nebula of thousands of fake accounts would then need to pay the time and compute cost for every single identity, while honest agents accumulate reputation that cannot be transferred or cheaply cloned. Forging one account is easy; forging a credible history for ten thousand is not.
